neighbours.label: the physical scene of clinical care: staff, garments and rooms on the ward (scrubs, gown, emergency room, gurney)
fire: The interns pulled on their scrubs and followed the senior doctor from bed to bed.
The boy sobbed on the gurney while the triage nurse looked for a vein.
Everyone entering the isolation ward must put on a mask and a paper gown.
My attending glanced over the chart and told me to page the surgical resident.
They wheeled him down the hall of the emergency department under bright lights.
Nurses in blue uniforms hurried past the curtain to the woman's bedside.
After the code, the exhausted residents sat in the call room in bloodstained clogs.
The dentist's assistant in a white coat laid the instruments out on the tray.
quiet: The journal reported that rates of the infection fell by a third over the decade.
The national board awarded the medical center its certificate for patient safety.
The disease is caused by a virus and usually clears up within two weeks.
Researchers reviewed forty trials of the drug and found only a modest benefit.
The textbook was edited by two neurologists and printed in Philadelphia in 2011.
The workers pulled on their overalls and followed the foreman from truck to truck.
The students in blue uniforms hurried past the gate to the science classroom.
The hairdresser's assistant in a black apron laid the combs out on the shelf.

notes: Output direction reversed promotes scr, chart, resident, OR, rounds. The + pole is institutional medicine (accreditation, citations), so near misses are medical but not a scene, or a scene outside medicine.
